newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to set up food centres in case of air embargo.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to set up food centres in case of air embargo.

text.p: Sudan will set up centres to sell basic goods at half their market price to prepare for a possible international air embargo, an official was quoted on Monday as saying.

Sudan's chamber of commerce will establish the 35 centres to sell some 12 goods in the capital Khartoum including sugar, edible oil, rice, soap, sorghum and lentils to face any problems, said the head of the chamber, Ali Hamid Abdel Rahman.
"This move comes within the general mobilisation to face the plans of siege against the Sudan," Rahman told the independent daily al-Rai al-Aam.

The U.N. Security Council last week delayed for a month a decision on implementing an air embargo against Sudan for failing to extradite three men wanted for an attempt to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa last year.

Sudan is hoping that the U.N. delay of the decision will give the world body time to reconsider the move. The African country is already the target of mandatory diplomatic and travel sanctions that went into effect on May 10.
The Sudanese government says it has complied with Security Council resolutions and provided all information available but says Egypt and Ethiopia have not cooperated.
It has denied supporting or facilitating terrorism.
